tree_choices.hypothesis: A TF-IDF feature union over word n-grams and character n-grams, paired with multinomial logistic regression using lbfgs and explicit random_state=7, will separate the three author classes by capturing both lexical and stylistic character patterns.

The failed configuration likely used broad word/character TF-IDF features with default multinomial logistic regularization, leaving noisy sparse features and poorly calibrated probabilities. A mechanism that selects TF-IDF min_df/max_df/ngram ranges and logistic regularization strength using train-only cross-validation, then refits on all training rows with sublinear TF, should reduce feature noise and regularization mismatch.

The prior sparse TF-IDF logistic pipeline likely underused author-specific orthographic and stylistic cues and produced overconfident probabilities. A feature union of word TF-IDF and character 3-5 gram TF-IDF, using sublinear term frequency and train-only selection of min_df/max_features, feeding multinomial logistic regression with C chosen by train-only CV and probabilities calibrated from out-of-fold folds, should capture both lexical and stylistic signals while reducing log-loss from miscalibration.

ideas.expected_observation: Validation negative log loss should improve over a single word-only representation because character n-grams model author-specific spelling, punctuation, and morphology.
ideas.hypothesis: A TF-IDF feature union over word n-grams and character n-grams, paired with multinomial logistic regression using lbfgs and explicit random_state=7, will separate the three author classes by capturing both lexical and stylistic character patterns.

ideas.expected_observation: The calibrated one-vs-rest SVM should yield finite per-row probabilities summing to 1 and competitive negative log loss, especially if character n-grams dominate author style.
ideas.hypothesis: A linear support vector classifier wrapped in OneVsRestClassifier with calibrated probability estimates, trained on TF-IDF character n-grams, will produce well-separated author probabilities suitable for multiclass log loss.

ideas.expected_observation: The ensemble should slightly improve negative log loss over either base model alone when both base models make complementary errors across author classes.
ideas.hypothesis: A soft-voting ensemble combining multinomial logistic regression and multinomial Naive Bayes over TF-IDF word and character n-grams will reduce variance in predicted class probabilities while preserving exact row_id coverage.

observation.task:
Write a COMPLETE executable Python program for a frozen CSV machine-learning task. It will run once in an isolated workspace with no network. Read data/protocol.json, data/train.csv and data/predict.csv. Train using only train.csv. Write predictions.csv with EXACT row_id coverage and the output columns declared below. The prediction table mixes anonymous validation and final submission rows; do not infer or select subsets. Classification output must be finite probabilities in [0,1] summing to 1 on each row; regression output must be finite and nonnegative. You may use installed numpy/pandas/scikit-learn, standard library, For multiclass logistic regression, use a compatible solver such as lbfgs, or explicitly wrap a binary estimator in OneVsRestClassifier. and the supplied CSV features. Set random seeds explicitly. Do not use internet, images or geometry files. Do not read other directories or launch persistent processes.
PROTOCOL:
{"features": ["text"], "kind": "classification", "output_columns": ["row_id", "EAP", "HPL", "MWS"], "output_file": "predictions.csv", "prediction_file": "predict.csv", "protocol": "mle-public-train-composed-v2", "row_id": "row_id", "seed": 7, "selection_metric": "negative_log_loss", "target_columns": ["target"], "task": "spooky-author-identification", "training_file": "train.csv"}
Select by maximum negative_log_loss; this is the negated task loss.

ideas.expected_observation: If the negative dev result was caused by feature noise or regularization mismatch, the cross-validated feature/regularization-selected logistic pipeline should produce finite well-calibrated probabilities and improve negative log loss over the default TF-IDF feature union.
ideas.hypothesis: The failed configuration likely used broad word/character TF-IDF features with default multinomial logistic regularization, leaving noisy sparse features and poorly calibrated probabilities. A mechanism that selects TF-IDF min_df/max_df/ngram ranges and logistic regularization strength using train-only cross-validation, then refits on all training rows with sublinear TF, should reduce feature noise and regularization mismatch.

ideas.expected_observation: If the plain TF-IDF logistic model failed due to diffuse lexical features, the NB-weighted linear classifier should produce better-separated author probabilities and improve negative log loss while preserving valid multiclass probability output.
ideas.hypothesis: Plain TF-IDF logistic regression may underfit because diffuse common n-grams dominate the feature space. Reweighting TF-IDF features by Naive Bayes log-count ratios before a linear classifier should emphasize discriminative author-style cues and suppress common n-grams, yielding better class separation.

ideas.expected_observation: If the model ranks author classes reasonably but assigns overconfident probabilities, cross-validated calibration should lower negative log loss and still output finite per-row probabilities summing to one.
ideas.hypothesis: The failed attempt may have had usable discrimination but overconfident or mis-normalized probabilities, causing poor negative log loss. A mechanism that trains a regularized linear classifier and calibrates its multiclass probability output using train-only cross-validation before normalization should reduce log-loss penalties from miscalibration.
